It applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL; this trip is RYDE_X, solo_optimal_distance_km is null, and no matched-itinerary optimal is recorded anywhere. The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 burden. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00534 and align on the 17:00–17:06 pickup window, and the excess of 2.73 km clears both POL-RD-01 limbs. The fare model on the breakdown is METERED and the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0, so recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 7.4 + 0.28 × 13.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. No pass-through line adds to or is netted against that figure. The fare breakdown itemises no ERP gantry, no toll and no airport surcharge — all are zero — and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a gantry, so POL-RD-09 yields no standalone correction and the refund stands at the 5.95 computed under POL-RD-02, with no line counted twice.

In any event no repeat pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days. The correct outcome on this record is the PARTIAL_REFUND of 5.95 under POL-RD-02.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you are broadly right about what happened, and the money follows arithmetic rather than blame.

ROUTE. The governing measurement is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00534): it runs 10.13 km against the booked optimal of 7.40 km, an excess of 2.73 km, or 36.89% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT a material deviation: 36.89% is below the 50% mark and 2.73 km is below the 8.0 km mark, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not engaged. In any event the driver's record shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days), so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise.

NO EXCULPATION. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00534-01, is MISSING (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); it carries no fact and its absence, not its content, is what is used, so it does not cap confidence. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot run and no closure-adjusted optimal can replace the booked 7.40 km. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00534) holds a single message, from the driver - 'setting off now' - with no waypoint, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction test has nothing to run against. No pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked 7.40 km stands.

THE SECOND PICKUP. The driver's statement that 'the second pickup was practically on the way' is accepted as an admission that the extra stop happened, and the rider's account of it is credited. But no clause of this policy excludes a non-rider-requested stop's distance from the excess, and this was not a pooled product, so it does not alter the arithmetic. 'She got to her destination on time' and 'nobody was harmed' engage no clause.

REMEDY (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 7.40 + 0.28 x 13.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 13.79. charged_total = 19.74. Refund = 19.74 - 13.79 = 5.95, which is 30.1% of the charge - above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% that would convert it to a full refund. No ERP, toll or surcharge line exists to add under POL-RD-09 (all itemised totals are 0.00, and the trip neither originates nor terminates at an airport), so nothing is counted twice.

The rider's request for the whole 19.74 is not supported: the recomputation deliberately retains the base fare and platform fee, and no clause refunds them. The outcome is a PARTIAL REFUND of SGD 5.95; the rest of the charge stands. No clause produces a referral in this case.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
